page: Amazon Web Services m9g.4xlarge is a general-purpose server instance powered by custom AWS Graviton processors. Built on the ARM64 architecture, it features 16 dedicated physical cores and 16 vCPUs utilizing the ARMv9 Neoverse-V3 model running at 2.8 GHz. The processor configuration includes a 64 KB L1d cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and 48 MB L3 cache, with hardware-accelerated AES cryptography support. It is equipped with 64.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced allocation of 4.0 GB per core.

This instance operates on the AWS Nitro hypervisor. It does not include local NVMe storage, meaning all storage requirements must be met via network-attached volumes. Network connectivity is defined by an 8 Gbps baseline bandwidth. The instance does not include complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark data indicates strong memory and compression capabilities. The Passmark memory score ranks in the top tier, supported by a read-only small block memory bandwidth of 2282.43 GB/sec. Single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression both achieve top-tier performance at 36.42 GB/sec and 17.14 GB/sec respectively. Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression and Passmark database operations also show strong performance. For machine learning workloads, the instance delivers top-tier text generation speeds of 376.71 tokens/second on small 135M LLM models and strong performance of 30.2 tokens/second on medium 7B models.

Given its dedicated ARMv9 core architecture and high memory bandwidth relative to its resource footprint, the m9g.4xlarge offers a highly resource-dense profile for general-purpose workloads. It is well-suited for database operations, static web serving, data compression tasks, and lightweight LLM inference. The lack of local storage and GPU acceleration represents a tradeoff, positioning this instance primarily for memory-bound and CPU-bound applications that rely on network storage.
